items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: The interviewer introduces John Steiner as the interviewer ('This is John Steiner. I'm interviewing Bob Lovett...'). The interviewee (Bob Lovett) does not mention John Steiner in his response, nor does he describe any personal or professional relationship with him.

ctx.x: This is John Steiner. I'm interviewing Bob Lovett, a clarinetist who admired and played in the New Orleans style in the 1948-49 period when he was a student at the University of Chicago. Bob was friendly with many of the New Orleans men who were around town and because of his intimate acquaintance with them, I thought that an interview might shed some light from the standpoint of a practicing musician who was not actually from New Orleans but who enjoyed the New Orleans influence and knew he did. We're…

Bob, when did you start playing clarinet? Probably when I was about 16, maybe 15 years old. That would have been around 1940 or 41. Where were you at the time? At that time I was in Boston, Massachusetts. Do you remember what influenced you to be interested in the clarinet? Yes, I was interested in jazz at that time. I had bought quite a few records. I had heard some Louis Armstrong records. In those days I wasn't very discriminating in my taste and I just sort of liked jazz in general.
